terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A parked vehicle prop: an exterior shell with no interior geometry, since a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside and the glazing is authored as a tinted, mostly opaque pane. The wheels are the mechanisms: each is a named pivot on its axle. Nothing else moves and nothing attaches, so there are no sockets. The best-selling vehicle in Thailand: a working double-cab pickup. The plate shows a muted blue extended cab with a quarter light behind the door, a chrome-barred grille between clear rectangular lamps over a black bumper, black wheel-arch flares, steel wheels caked in tan mud, mud sprayed up the lower doors and sills, and a short open bed with a dark liner.

reasoning: The identity is the side profile -- bonnet, raked screen, cab, open bed -- and it is one closed polygon swept across the width, with the wheel arches cut into it as notches, then narrowed above the belt for tumblehome. One geometry carries the whole shell.
One repetition system: four wheels off one lathe, each a named pivot on its axle.

Three materials, because a colour difference is not a material difference: the paint carries the mud envelope with the clean blue on a canvas tile, and every trim tone -- tyre, rim, bumper, lamp, liner -- is a vertex colour on one white material.
Action readiness is the wheels: four hinge pivots, convex collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: A pickup cannot be a box on a box: the raked screen, the tumblehome and the arches are what make it read as a truck at prop distance, and all three come from shaping one extrusion. The bed is open, so its walls, bulkhead and tailgate are boxes merged into the same shell, and the glasshouse is a second extrusion of the cab polygon offset 6 mm proud so no pane shares a plane with the body.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 1.86 x 1.82 x 5.33 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=8000 triangles, <=6 draw calls, <=4 materials, <=8 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus one named pivot per wheel (4); zero sockets; convex collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center at tyre contact, +Y up, +Z FORWARD, +X the vehicle's left. Meshy returned the proxy with its long axis on X, an arbitrary output convention; the band comparison detects the mismatch from the two footprints and rotates the reference a quarter turn before measuring.

silhouette.description: Sill at 0.42 m, wheels 0.75 m in diameter at z +1.715 and -1.37 (3.085 wheelbase, 0.95 front overhang), bonnet lip at 0.86-0.94 m rising to a scuttle at 1.08 m, windscreen raked from z 1.45 to a roof at 1.80 m over 0.12 m corner arcs, a vertical cab back at z -0.72 dropping to a bed floor at 0.80 m, bed rails at 1.20 m to a tailgate at z -2.60. Roof width 0.83 of the body. The silhouette events are the nose, the raked screen, the cab step down to the bed and the two arches. Sheet metal crowns over a 0.13 m shoulder fillet from the cab back to the top of the rake and wraps a 0.24 m plan radius at the nose (0.06 at the tail).
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.93..+0.93 on the body shell (the door mirrors reach +-1.03 and are reported, as a real Hilux is 1.855 m over the body and ~2.1 over its mirrors); y 0.00 (tyre contact) to 1.80 (roof); z -2.665..+2.665 bumper to bumper, +Z forward. The registry declares the real vehicle; the Meshy proxy normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.437 : 0.448, a truck only 2.29 lengths tall, so heights were read off the proxy as fractions of H and stations as fractions of L, and the declared metres win on both axes.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to L:H:W = 1 : 0.437 : 0.448 -- a truck 2.29 lengths tall against the real 2.93. The area-weighted band table (scratch/_mon/bands.mjs) therefore reads a mean |delta depth| of 0.44 of height that is almost entirely that declared aspect: at bands 2-5 the proxy's depth is 2.04-2.16 H and the candidate's 2.76-2.86 H, and 5.33 / 1.82 = 2.93. The proxy's heights agree with the plate (roof 1.00 H, belt and bed rail 0.66 H, wheel top 0.40 H, sill 0.26 H) and are what was built. Its cab width at the top three bands (0.72-0.80 H) is narrower than the first build's 0.94, which is why the tumblehome was deepened to 0.17.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.75: the plate shows the front three-quarter and the bed from above; the tailgate face, its lamps and the rear bumper are built to the type (a plain tailgate with vertical lamps either side) and to the proxy's rear elevation.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/paint.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.751. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.evidence: Sill crop #8b8075 against the roof's #385176. Delivered as a wash rising from the ground to 0.36 of a 2 m height-keyed tile plus ninety soft blobs above it, all at the envelope colour, on a base that is the clean ratio. Height-keyed UVs keep the roof clean.

evidence: Clean paint measured on viewEvidence region-paint (the roof, PBR confidence 0.751) at #385176; the mud on the sill (region-sill, 520..580 x 690..720) measures #8b8075 and is BRIGHTER than the paint in every channel, so the material carries the MUD ENVELOPE and the clean blue is painted back as the linear-space ratio (0.43, 0.65, 1.00) of it on a post-construction canvas.
Textureless as DECLARED: the mud is a seamless 512 px Canvas 2D tile bound after material construction as map, so no procedural texture set is synthesised. Body vertex colours are white.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout: three components and one InstancedMesh at 4 draw calls of 6, costed before geometry existed.
Bed rail cap had been authored full width and sealed the bed; split into two side caps and a tailgate cap. Tumblehome deepened 0.10 -> 0.17 on the band table.

Second pass (user review): the shell was a slab -- hard roof corners, a box nose, and a plan taper folded across one flat-shaded cap triangle per outline edge, which drew a diagonal crease from the bonnet lip to the sill on both front fenders. Rebuilt on the shaped template: bonnet-lip and roof-corner arcs in the outline, shoulder fillet r 0.13 from the cab back to the top of the rake, plan nose r 0.24 and tail r 0.06, 14 edge-biased width columns, 50-degree smooth normals. Crease gone at 0, 90, 180 and 270; check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Three components and one repetition system: 4 of 6. The bed and the pillars ride the shell; forty trim parts ride one merge.

materials.note: paint, glass and a white vertex-coloured trim: 3 of 4. Tyres, rims, bumpers, lamps and the liner differ in albedo only.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 4,568 of 8,000: one extrusion with two 8-segment arches over 14 width columns, four pillar strips, a 20-segment wheel lathe, and boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A closed side-profile polygon extruded across the width in 14 edge-biased columns and shaped per vertex (tumblehome above the belt, plan taper, a shoulder fillet along the roof edge, plan-radius nose and tail, angle-limited smooth normals); an offset extrusion of the cab polygon for the glass; a lathe for the wheel; boxes for everything else.
One InstancedMesh carries the four wheels; the right-side instances are yawed a half turn so the dish faces out. No per-instance colour, so the white base is inert.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. ONE 512 px Canvas 2D mud tile is bound after construction as the paint map: base is the clean-paint ratio of the mud envelope formed in linear space, mud is a wash and soft blobs at the envelope. 1.3 MB of texture VRAM, factory 86 ms.

risks.description: The proxy is 2.29 lengths tall; the real truck is 2.93. The band table's depth residual is that ratio.
risks.mitigation: Declared metres win; heights and stations were read off the proxy as fractions. Reported with the arithmetic.

risks.description: The tailgate face and rear lamps are built to type.
Plate shows an extended cab; registry text says double cab.
